items.note: Lab study (N=20) comparing the IdeaSynth research-ideation system with a strong LLM baseline (AI configuration vs AI configuration); outcomes are number of alternative ideas explored and idea detail, not rated creativity; below 50 participants; plus a 7-person deployment study.

Between-subjects experiment (N=79) varying the automation level (low, moderate, high) of a generative AI design tool; outcomes include time, creative experience, and creative quality (aesthetics, usability) of the designs; no no-AI arm, and random assignment is not stated.

Platform paper (Epitome) that validates itself by replicating three experiments; search notes say one is a Doshi and Hauser (2024) story-writing replication with 0, 1, or 5 AI ideas and expert-rated originality and diversity, but the abstract does not describe it or give the sample size; check the full text.

Within-subjects study (N=20) comparing a multi-agent ideation system (MultiColleagues) with a single-agent baseline; quality and novelty are rated by participants themselves, elaboration may be coded from the ideation logs; below 50 participants; same work as arXiv 2510.23904.

Classroom study: 50 undergraduates divided into AI-supported and non-AI teams for the Alternative Uses Task, scored on fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration; assignment method not stated and the unit may be teams.

Evaluative study comparing design inspiration boards made with image-generative AI and with traditional methods on diversity, quantity, fidelity, and ambiguity; the abstract does not say whether participants made the boards under assigned conditions, so it may instead be an AI-versus-human output comparison.

Reanalysis of the DesignAID experiment (Cai et al. 2023; 2x2 factorial, 111 of 115 participants per the full text, Direct vs Diverse LLM idea modes) with a semantic-area metric; people who saw more diverse AI ideas selected more diverse but less innovative ideas per evaluators; abstract taken from the ICCC PDF (no DOI); shares its sample with the DesignAID paper.

Ideation workshop with design-student teams on whether GenAI helps overcome creative fixation, examining team dynamics and creative results; the abstract states no comparison condition or sample size, so it may be a descriptive workshop study.

Controlled study with 25 design students comparing GPT-4 feedback with feedback from six human educators during brainstorming (AI vs human aid); reported outcomes are motivation and iterative idea refinement, with no rated creativity mentioned; below 50 participants.

Lab experiment randomly assigning 58 participants to a creative product design task with or without ChatGPT; the abstract reports only psychological ownership and idea championing, so check the full text for any rating of idea creativity (otherwise out: no creativity outcome); AOM poster proceedings.
